title: Stroopwafels
subtitle: Dutch syrup waffle cookies sandwiched with caramel syrup
excerpt: Stroopwafels are thin, crisp Dutch waffles sandwiched with a sticky caramel syrup filling. You get a biscuit that softens slightly when held over a hot drink, which is the traditional way to eat them. The waffles are made on an electric waffle iron, not in the oven.
sourceNotes: Stroopwafels (syrup waffles) originate in Gouda, Netherlands, where they were first made by baker Gerard Kamphuisen around 1810. They are made by pressing a yeasted dough in a waffle iron and sandwiching the thin waffle rounds with a stroop (syrup and caramel) filling.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unfilled waffle rounds. Sandwich with syrup filling after defrosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough needs 1 hour to rest before cooking. Make the syrup filling while the dough rests. Finished stroopwafels keep in an airtight tin for up to 5 days.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Electric waffle iron at medium-high heat. No oven required.

glossaryTerms.definition: An electric appliance with two hinged plates that press and cook a dough or batter between them, imprinting a grid pattern. For stroopwafels, the plates are smooth or have a shallow waffle pattern, and the iron cooks the dough quickly at high heat. The waffles are split horizontally while still warm and pliable; once cooled they become crisp and rigid.

The thick, sticky filling of a stroopwafel: butter, soft brown sugar, golden syrup, and cinnamon cooked together until the mixture reaches the soft-ball stage (around 115 degrees Celsius). The filling must be used while still warm and spreadable; it thickens to a firm caramel as it cools and sets the two waffle halves together.

content.text: Dissolve the dried yeast in the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes until foamy. In a large bowl, combine the flour, caster sugar, and cinnamon. Add the melted butter, egg, and yeast mixture. Mix to a soft, smooth dough. Cover the bowl and leave at room temperature for 1 hour until the dough has puffed slightly.

Combine the soft brown sugar, butter, golden syrup, and cinnamon in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the butter has melted and the mixture is smooth. Continue cooking to 115 degrees Celsius on a sugar thermometer (soft-ball stage), which takes about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. The filling will thicken as it cools; keep it warm by leaving the pan in a bowl of hot water while you cook the waffles.

Heat the electric waffle iron to medium-high. Divide the dough into balls of about 30 g each. Place one ball in the centre of the waffle iron and close the lid. Cook for 90 seconds to 2 minutes. The waffle should be golden on both sides; open the iron and check the colour at 90 seconds.

Remove the waffle immediately and, working quickly while it is still warm and pliable, split it horizontally through the middle using a serrated knife or a thin blade. If the waffle cools before you split it, it will snap rather than separate cleanly.

Spread a generous layer of warm caramel syrup on the cut side of the base half. Press the top half firmly onto the filling. Hold together for 10 to 15 seconds while the caramel begins to set. Place on a rack to cool and firm completely.
Repeat with the remaining dough. If the syrup filling thickens too much as you work, briefly warm the pan over low heat to loosen it.

attrs.problem: The waffles crack and snap when trying to split them
attrs.avoid: Avoid letting the waffle cool before splitting; once cool it is rigid and cannot be separated.
attrs.fix: Work directly from the waffle iron to the splitting board without pausing. Have your knife ready. If a waffle cools before you split it, return it briefly to the closed waffle iron for 20 seconds to soften slightly, then split immediately.

attrs.problem: The syrup filling is too thick to spread
attrs.avoid: Avoid making the filling too far ahead and letting it cool fully before you start cooking waffles.
attrs.fix: Keep the saucepan in a bowl of hot water throughout the process. If the filling is too thick, return it to the hob over very low heat for 30 seconds, stirring to loosen.

attrs.problem: The waffles are pale and doughy in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid undercooking on the waffle iron; the inside of the ball of dough needs to cook through.
attrs.fix: Cook for the full 2 minutes. The outside will be golden; the inside will finish cooking from the residual heat. If the waffles are consistently pale, increase the waffle iron temperature setting and reduce the ball size slightly.
